name: Vintage Digital
description: The converters of an early sampler: a sample rate reducer and bit crusher with true aliasing, hold images, companding and clock jitter, from a soft twelve-bit glaze to folded metal.

params.name: Rate
params.description: The sample rate of the old converter. Lower is duller and grittier and brings ringing copies of the sound down into hearing. All the way up switches resampling off.

params.name: Bits
params.description: How finely the level is measured. Fewer bits add a grain that follows the sound, and quiet tails break up and then cut off.

params.name: Companding
params.description: How the steps are spaced. Linear has the same grain at every level, so quiet sounds suffer most. Mu-law packs the steps near silence, so quiet stays clean.

params.name: Aliasing
params.description: How much of the sound above half the Rate gets past the input filter. At zero the result is clean and dull. Turned up, those highs fold down as out-of-tune tones.

params.name: Filter
params.description: The filter after the converter. None leaves every stair step in, bright and glassy. Soft rounds them off. Steep removes everything above half the Rate, smooth and dull.

params.name: Jitter
params.description: Unsteadiness in the converter clock. It adds a hiss that rides on the sound, more on high notes than low ones, and none in silence.

params.name: Drive
params.description: Level into the converter. More uses more of its range, so the grain drops away, until peaks hit the top and clip flat. The output is turned down to match.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the clean signal and the converted one. Part way layers the grit under the untouched sound.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Models a sampling converter pair in outline (an input stage that clips, an anti-alias filter that can be taken away, a sampler on a jittery clock, a linear or mu-law quantiser, a zero-order hold and a reconstruction filter), not any one machine. The input is read between host samples with a 32-point windowed sinc and each change of the held value is drawn as a band-limited step from a table (the idea behind the kit's PolyBLEP oscillators), so the hold's images are kept and next to nothing folds back that a converter would not make. The steep filters are a ninth-order elliptic low-pass built as two allpass chains; its poles were computed for this device. No dither and no noise floor: silence in is exact silence out. Reports 129 samples of latency: 33 for the clip, the interpolation and the band-limited step, and 96 so the converted signal's low end can be lined up with the dry signal, so a part-way Mix does not comb below the converter's band (a narrow dip remains at the band's edge).
